name: Sun
description: The star at the center of our Solar System.

name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet in the Solar System.

name: BepiColombo
description: Europe's first mission to Mercury.
ou_involvement: The CEI provided the MIXS instrument.

name: Venus
description: Second planet from the Sun.

name: Earth
description: Our home planet.

name: ISS
description: The International Space Station, a modular space station in low Earth orbit.
ou_involvement: Materials Science: The OU has flown experiments to expose materials to the harsh space environment.

name: Hubble
description: A legendary space telescope that has revolutionized astronomy.
ou_involvement: Detector Heritage: The CCD technology in WFC3 shares heritage with CEI-characterized sensors.

name: Sentinel-5P
description: Map trace gases (NO2, O3, CH4) and pollution plumes with high resolution.
ou_involvement: Detector Testing: Radiation testing of TROPOMI CCDs; characterized 'hot pixels' and RTS noise.

name: Sentinel-2
description: High-res optical imagery for land monitoring, vegetation health, and crop stages.
ou_involvement: Characterisation: Analyzed radiation hardness of MSI CMOS/CCD detectors to ensure linearity.

name: Sentinel-3
description: Ocean colour measurements and climate monitoring; continuation of Envisat legacy.
ou_involvement: Calibration: Supported detector calibration for the OLCI instrument to detect faint phytoplankton signals.

name: CASTOR
description: Wide-field UV/Optical telescope to survey the cosmos, led by Canada.
ou_involvement: Science: OU researchers are involved in the science working groups for UV surveys.

name: TRUTHS
description: Establish a 'gold standard' for climate measurements to cross-calibrate other satellites.
ou_involvement: Metrology: Ultra-precise electro-optical characterisation of the Hyperspectral Imaging Spectrometer.

name: SMILE
description: Image Earth's magnetosphere in soft X-rays to understand solar wind interactions.
ou_involvement: Radiation Modelling: Qualified CCDs and 'notch' pixel architecture to survive Van Allen belt crossings.

name: Swift
description: Study Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) and their afterglows.
ou_involvement: Calibration Heritage: Played a fundamental role in calibrating the CCD-22 technology used in the XRT.

name: UKube-1
description: Technology demonstration for CubeSats and commercial off-the-shelf sensors.
ou_involvement: Instrument Lead: Provided the C3D (Compact CMOS Camera Demonstrator) to test radiation durability.

name: Chandrayaan-1
description: Mapped lunar surface elements (Mg, Al, Si) and tested the Lunar Magma Ocean hypothesis.
ou_involvement: Science Lead (C1XS): Collaborated on the X-ray Spectrometer to map elemental abundance.

name: Chang'e-5
description: Historic sample return mission delivering 1.7kg of lunar basalt to Earth.
ou_involvement: Sample Analysis: The OU is analyzing oxygen isotopes in the returned samples to understand lunar volcanism.

name: Luna 27
description: Analyzing lunar polar ice origin (cometary vs solar) and demonstrating water extraction (ISRU).
ou_involvement: Lead Institute (ProSPA): Leading the development of the ProSPA chemical lab to heat and analyze regolith.

name: LUPEX
description: Measuring pressure and composition of the lunar exosphere in permanently shadowed regions.
ou_involvement: Instrument Lead: Developing the EMS-L (Exospheric Mass Spectrometer) to 'sniff' the lunar atmosphere.

name: Earth-Sun L2
description: Lagrange Point 2

name: JWST
description: The premier space observatory of the next decade.
ou_involvement: MIRI: CEI researchers performed vital radiation damage testing on the detectors for the MIRI instrument.

name: Gaia
description: Gaia is creating a 3D map of the Milky Way.
ou_involvement: CEI researchers work on transient analysis.

name: Euclid
description: Map dark universe geometry via weak lensing and galaxy clustering.
ou_involvement: Detector Science: Led radiation characterisation for VIS CCDs; developed 'trap pumping' correction models.

name: Athena
description: Study the hot, energetic universe (black holes, galaxy clusters) via X-ray spectroscopy.
ou_involvement: Z-Shielding: Designing the Graded Z-shield to block cosmic ray noise from reaching the WFI detector.

name: HWO
description: Habitable Worlds Observatory. A flagship mission to image Earth-like exoplanets.
ou_involvement: Future Technology: Contributing to the definition of detector requirements for ultra-low noise imaging.

name: PLATO
description: Detect Earth-sized habitable planets by monitoring star brightness (transits).
ou_involvement: CCD Stability: Characterizing electro-optical performance of CCD270s to ensure photometric stability.

name: Roman
description: Wide-field Hubble to image exoplanets directly and study dark energy.
ou_involvement: EMCCD Tech: Enhancing Electron-Multiplying CCD technology for radiation tolerance in space.

name: Mars
description: The Red Planet.

name: ExoMars TGO
description: Searching for trace gases.
ou_involvement: The CEI leads the NOMAD instrument.

name: Beagle 2
description: Detect life via isotopic analysis; searching for a preference for Carbon-12 in Martian soil.
ou_involvement: Built GAP: Designed and built the Gas Analysis Package (mass spectrometer & oven) to analyse soil.

name: Perseverance
description: Exploring Jezero Crater.
ou_involvement: CEI validates SHERLOC sensors.

name: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin
description: Drill 2m deep to search for biomarkers and signs of past life protected from radiation.
ou_involvement: PanCam & Geology: Co-PI for Panoramic Camera; led geological mapping and selection of Oxia Planum site.

name: MSL Curiosity
description: Explore Gale Crater for habitable ancient environments and analyze fluid chemistry.
ou_involvement: Science Team: Thermochemical modelling of mudstones/minerals to determine ancient water pH and salinity.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet.

name: JUICE
description: JUpiter ICy moons Explorer. Performing complex gravity assists (Earth-Venus-Earth-Earth) to reach Jupiter in July 2031.
ou_involvement: Sensor Valid.: Validated CMOS sensors for the JANUS camera system using data from UKube-1.

name: Saturn
description: Famous for its rings.

name: Cassini
description: The mission that revolutionized our understanding of the Saturnian system.
ou_involvement: Lander Tech: The OU designed and built the Surface Science Package (SSP) on the attached Huygens probe.

name: Huygens
description: The first and only landing in the outer solar system.
ou_involvement: Sensors: The OU developed the Surface Science Package (SSP) to measure Titan's physical properties.

name: Rosetta
description: Analyze comet composition and volatiles to understand the origin of water on Earth.
ou_involvement: PI for Ptolemy: Led the gas analyser instrument on the Philae lander; measured D/H ratio of comet water.

name: Philae
description: Philae lander on 67P.

name: Hera
description: Assess the aftermath of the DART impactor on asteroid Dimorphos for planetary defence.
ou_involvement: Investigation Team: Asteroid dynamics and thermal modelling to interpret physical properties and mass.

name: AKARI
description: Japanese infrared astronomy satellite that surveyed the entire sky.
ou_involvement: Science: OU researchers used AKARI data to study interstellar dust and star formation.

name: Spitzer
description: Infrared Great Observatory that discovered the 'TRAPPIST-1' exoplanets.
ou_involvement: Exoplanets: OU scientists analyze Spitzer light curves to characterize exoplanet atmospheres.

name: Herschel
description: The largest infrared telescope ever flown; studied the coolest objects in the universe.
ou_involvement: SPIRE Instrument: The OU was a co-investigator institute for the SPIRE camera/spectrometer.

name: Planck
description: Mapped the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) with unprecedented precision.
ou_involvement: Science: Used Planck data to study galaxy clusters and the early universe structure.

name: Peregrine
description: First private US lunar lander (Astrobotic). It suffered a propellant leak and re-entered Earth's atmosphere.
ou_involvement: Instrument: The OU developed the Exospheric Mass Spectrometer (PITMS) to measure the lunar exosphere.

name: Comet Interceptor
description: A mission to ambush a pristine, long-period comet entering the inner solar system for the first time.
ou_involvement: Instruments: The OU is providing the focal plane arrays for the Modular X-ray Source (MIXS) heritage instrument.

name: EnVision
description: High-resolution radar mapping and atmospheric monitoring to understand why Earth's twin became so inhospitable.
ou_involvement: Instrument Co-I: The OU is involved in the VenSpec-H spectrometer to study the atmosphere and volcanic gases.

name: OGRE
description: Off-plane Grating Rocket Experiment. A sub-orbital sounding rocket to capture the highest resolution soft X-ray spectrum of Capella.
ou_involvement: Detectors: The CEI developed the EMCCD camera system to survive the violent vibration of a rocket launch.

name: Hayabusa2
description: Japanese mission that deploy rovers and returned samples from Ryugu.
ou_involvement: Sample Analysis: OU researchers analyzed the returned Ryugu grains to study water and organics.

name: OSIRIS-REx
description: Returned a massive sample from asteroid Bennu; now renamed OSIRIS-APEX to study Apophis.
ou_involvement: Sample Analysis: The OU is analyzing the Bennu samples to investigate the early solar system's chemistry.

name: Stardust
description: The first mission to return cometary dust (from Comet Wild 2) to Earth.
ou_involvement: Sample Analysis: The OU led the analysis of the cometary dust tracks in the aerogel collector.

name: Bennu
description: A carbonaceous, diamond-shaped near-Earth asteroid.

name: Ryugu
description: A diamond-shaped near-Earth asteroid sampled by Hayabusa2.

name: Comet Wild 2
description: A lumpy comet visited by Stardust in 2004.

name: Earth-Sun L1
description: Lagrange Point 1

name: Genesis
description: Collected solar wind samples. The return capsule crash-landed in Utah, but the samples were successfully recovered.
ou_involvement: Oxygen Isotopes: OU researchers used the NanoSIMS to analyze the returned samples, revealing the Sun's oxygen isotopic composition.
